item.description:
STORY | Willing to accept results: Trump after facing midterm reversals

US President Donald Trump has said he was willing to accept the results of the mid-term elections, where Democrats posted significant gains, flipping key Senate and gubernatorial races.

“I am absolutely willing to accept those results,” Trump said in an interview with The New York Times on Tuesday night as results trickled in.

Democrats had wrested the US Senate races in Texas, North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio – states where Trump campaigned hard, urging voters to pretend that he was on the ballot.

Trump told the New York Times that he was prepared to work with Democrats.

“We'll work with the Democrats, and we'll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out,” the President said, days after claiming that he would run the administration over the next two years using his veto powers.

Trump blamed Republican losses on the fact that he was not on the ballot and said he had no regrets about endorsing candidates such as Senator Darline Graham, Republican of South Carolina, and Ken Paxton, the Republican attorney general of Texas.

“I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump posted on Truth Social.

(Report by Sagar Kulkarni/PTI)

item.description:
STORY | 'Delhi's AQI at 'very poor'; Punjabi Bagh worst at 458'

Delhi's air quality was in the 'very poor' category again on Wednesday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) at 379, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).

Punjabi Bagh recorded the worst air quality at 458, falling in the 'severe' category.

The city’s AQI breached the 300-mark on Tuesday also, when it stood at 332, falling into the ‘very poor’ category.

According to the CPCB, an AQI between zero and 50 is classified as good, 51 and 100 as satisfactory, 101 and 200 as moderate, 201 and 300 as poor, 301 and 400 as very poor, and 401 and 500 as severe.

Amid the toxic air, the minimum temperature at Safdarjung, Delhi's primary weather station, settled at 16.1 degrees Celsius on Wednesday, 0.8 degrees above the season's average, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

Among the other weather stations, Palam recorded a minimum temperature of 16.9 degrees Celsius, 0.7 degrees above normal. Lodhi Road settled at 16.1 degrees Celsius, 3.1 degrees above normal, while the Ridge station recorded 16.4 degrees Celsius, 0.7 degrees below normal.

Ayanagar recorded a minimum temperature of 16.6 degrees Celsius, 0.4 degrees above the seasonal average.

No rainfall was recorded at any of the five weather stations during the 24-hour period ending at 8.30 am on Wednesday.

item.description:
VIDEO | US Midterm Polls: Residents in Georgia glued to television as results start trickling in. Democrats made significant gains in the US mid-term elections, flipping the gubernatorial race in Georgia and positioning themselves to wrest key Senate seats from Republicans, delivering a stinging rebuke to President Donald Trump.

A resident in Georgia said, "While it is too early to call, the results have been quite encouraging for the Democrats. There is at least one Senate seat that has been flipped in North Carolina, which is a good sign for them. As far as overall control of the Senate goes, there is still a long way to go, though the projections look pretty good for the Democrats. Overall, I think it is a good night for them."

Asked if it would be good news if the Democratic Party manages to control both the House and the Senate, he said, "Possibly, because that would act as a check on presidential powers, which, in my opinion, have gone unchecked for the last two years. It would restore a balance of power between Congress (the House and Senate) and the executive branch led by the President. That would be good for the country because, as I noticed at the polls this morning, the majority of Americans prefer a centrist approach rather than political extremes."

Another resident said, "As someone mentioned this morning, it is especially important for voters seeking a moderate, middle-ground approach, neither too far right nor too far left, to step up. Checks and balances are essential for a viable, functioning democracy, and having a midterm election to readjust and recalibrate is very healthy for the democratic process."

item.description:
STORY | Delhi Police files FIR against Prashant Bhushan over fake Russian foreign minister video

Delhi Police has registered an FIR against senior Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan for sharing a digitally manipulated video of Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, which purportedly contained remarks hostile to India, officials said.

The case was registered at the Special Cell police station following cyber patrolling on November 3, when police noticed a social media post by the handle @thequotesnews, claiming that a purported doctored video of the foreign minister had been shared from Bhushan's X handle.

The video allegedly carried misleading and inflammatory content, with the potential to spread rumours, defame individuals and disturb public order, police said.

An FIR has been registered under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with the Information Technology Act.

The development comes after the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) fact-checked the digitally manipulated video falsely attributed to the Russian foreign minister.

The fabricated clip purportedly showed him making remarks critical of India over its internal affairs and oil purchases.

Police are investigating the matter and examining the content and its circulation on social media.

item.description:
VIDEO | Delhi: On health risks due to air pollution and ways to stay safe, Senior Consultant at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Dr Mohsin Wali says, "The implementation of Graded Response Action Plan has made everyone realise that the danger is there. Pollution is a perpetual problem, an issue we face every year that severe during this season... While pollution persists throughout the year, we talk about it more right now because of this sudden spike. Pollution causes severe trouble for asthma patients, diabetic individuals, obese patients, high blood pressure patients, heart patients, young children, and the elderly. Pollution does not merely stay in the nose; it enters deep into the lungs. The microplastics present in polluted air are causing extensive damage. These microparticles are so minute that they even enter the bloodstream. Only green firecrackers should be allowed during Diwali, and the government must make proper arrangements for this."

On ways to tackle air pollution, he says, "Practice deep breathing, regular exercise, yoga and any respiratory exercises. Avoid going for a morning run, get regular sleep, eat simple food, drink plenty of water, and frequently wash your nose and hands. Pollution harms the lungs, reaches the liver, and damages the kidneys as well..."

🚨 SOUTH KOREA INVESTIGATES PRESIDENTIAL DELEGATION DATA EXPOSED ON VIRUSTOTAL

KBS says it found a spreadsheet on VirusTotal containing passport details and other personal data for 168 people, including President Lee Jae Myung, the first lady and members of his protection team.

* KBS dates the upload to June 2 and confirmed the file's removal after contacting the platform.
* On Nov 3, the presidential office ordered an investigation and a review of overseas-trip security.
* The Foreign Ministry is treating the incident as a data leak; passport reissuance is underway.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The uploader and anyone who may have downloaded copies are unknown, and the cause remains under investigation. No intrusion into VirusTotal has been reported; June is the reported exposure date, not a new November breach.

Practical warning: check how an external scanning service retains and shares submissions before uploading sensitive documents.

item.description:
Police seized more than 100 servers in a crackdown on a suspected supplier of investment-scam websites.

Eurojust says today's German-led operation searched 17 locations and arrested seven suspects for surrender or extradition to Germany.

* Investigators allege a company operating from Cyprus and Israel supplied fake trading websites to multiple criminal groups.
* Suspected customers ran call centers in Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia.
* Fake account profits and pressure from supposed brokers encouraged victims to send more money. Withdrawals were then blocked.
* Authorities estimate losses above €4 million. The final scale and any money recovered for victims remain unclear.

The operation targets shared infrastructure behind multiple fraud schemes, following earlier actions in 2022 and 2025.

The seven arrests are not convictions, and the investigation continues.

https://www.eurojust.europa.eu/news/international-investment-fraud-scheme-dismantled-seven-arrests
#Cybercrime #InvestmentFraud

item.description:
🇨🇱 🚨 RANSOMWARE GROUP CLAIMS CHILEAN STATE OIL COMPANY ENAP'S EGYPT UNIT

The Aoqin ransomware group has listed Petroshahd, described as the Egypt branch of Enap Sipetrol International, on its leak site.

Enap Sipetrol is the international exploration and production arm of ENAP, Chile's state-owned oil and gas company, founded in 1950 and headquartered in Las Condes.

The group has not disclosed the size or type of the data it claims. ENAP has not publicly confirmed an incident, and the claim has not been verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
A hit on a state-owned energy company's overseas operation can expose joint-venture, contract and field data and open a path for follow-on phishing against partners. Partners of the Egypt operation should watch for ENAP-themed phishing and payment-change requests. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

item.description:
🏨 🚨 HACKER GROUP CLAIMS BREACH OF IHG HOTELS & RESORTS

A group calling itself "byod" has listed IHG Hotels & Resorts, the owner of Holiday Inn, Crowne Plaza, Six Senses, Staybridge Suites and Candlewood, on its leak site.

The group claims customer data, guest booking and folio records (names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, stay dates, rates and charges), loyalty program data, complete employee PII, AWS keys, Active Directory access, full access to CyberArk and all financial records. It says it got in through a weak LDAP binding password.

IHG has not publicly confirmed an incident, and the data has not been verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
If real, guest folio and loyalty data would fuel convincing booking-themed phishing and loyalty-points fraud across IHG brands. Guests should be wary of unexpected "reservation" or "payment update" messages and watch loyalty accounts. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

🇧🇷 ⚠️ BRAZIL: ACTOR CLAIMS 250 MILLION RECORDS FROM DETRAN TRAFFIC DEPARTMENT DATA

A threat actor on a dark web forum claims to hold a database of 250 million records said to come from DETRAN, Brazil's state traffic department system.

* Full names
* CPF national taxpayer ID numbers
* Places of birth

⚠️ Analyst Note:
OLD NEWS: the forum post appears to date from July 2026, so this may be recirculating rather than a new breach, and the 250 million figure is larger than Brazil's population, which suggests duplicates or merged older data. CPF numbers are still key to identity fraud and phishing in Brazil. DETRAN has not confirmed a breach that we are aware of. Unverified threat-actor claim.

🇷🇺 ⚠️ RUSSIA: ACTOR CLAIMS 100M+ RECORDS FROM THE PENSION FUND OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION

A threat actor on a dark web forum has posted a dataset they say comes from the Pension Fund of the Russian Federation (PFR), claiming more than 100 million records in about 45 GB of CSV files, with samples shared.

The post claims:
* SNILS pension insurance numbers and INN tax IDs
* Full names, dates of birth and partial passport numbers
* Phone numbers, emails and home addresses
* Employment history and bank account details

⚠️ Analyst Note:
OLD NEWS: the forum post appears to date from January 2026 and the data is described as 2025 records, so this may be recirculated rather than a fresh breach. If genuine, SNILS and tax IDs together with bank details are a strong base for identity theft and fraud against Russian citizens. Russian authorities have not confirmed a breach that we are aware of. Unverified threat-actor claim.

🇬🇧 🚨 DYSON: THREAT ACTOR ADVERTISES ALLEGED EMPLOYEE AND CORPORATE DATA ON DARK WEB FORUM

A threat actor on a dark web forum is selling two data packages they claim were stolen from Dyson, the UK technology and appliance maker. Each package is said to be roughly 65 GB to 255 GB.

The listing claims:
* Employee and manager credentials, bank details, personal IDs and biometric data
* Customer and employee emails
* Internal meeting recordings and legal and compliance dossiers
* Device clones with messaging data, plus API keys and passkeys

⚠️ Analyst Note:
If genuine, the mix of credentials, API keys and HR records would put Dyson staff at risk of identity fraud and targeted phishing, and could expose internal systems. The seller says some packages have already sold. Dyson has not confirmed an incident that we are aware of. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.

item.description:
🇷🇺 🚨 RUSSIA: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS LEAK OF FSB BORDER SERVICE DATA ON 1.5M TRAVELERS

A threat actor claims to be leaking 1.5 million records it says come from Russia's FSB Border Service, covering border crossings in 2026.

According to the actor:
• About 1.5 million records (claimed)
• Full names, years of birth and passport data (claimed)
• Border-crossing dates and times from January to September 1, 2026 (claimed)

No price or forum link was given, and we found no statement from Russian authorities.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a new FSB breach. A much larger "Kordon" border-crossing database (2014–2023) has circulated on forums since 2024, so this set could be a repackaged or partial copy rather than a fresh intrusion. If genuine, passport and travel records would carry surveillance and fraud risk for travelers, including foreign nationals.

item.title: 🇪🇸 🚨 SPAIN: MORTEMTEAM CLAIMS LEAK OF SPANISH GOVERNMENT DATA WITH 50M+ RECORDS The MortemTeam group claims it has breached "Spanish governme...
item.description:
🇪🇸 🚨 SPAIN: MORTEMTEAM CLAIMS LEAK OF SPANISH GOVERNMENT DATA WITH 50M+ RECORDS

The MortemTeam group claims it has breached "Spanish government" data and posted what it calls a 2TB database with more than 50 million records on a dark web forum.

According to the group:
• More than 50 million records, described as 2026 data (claimed)
• Total size of about 2TB (claimed)
• Personal data plus photos of identity documents (claimed)
• The data is being loaded into the group's paid lookup bot, which it says also covers Peru, Brazil, the US, Mexico, Chile, Colombia and other countries

The post does not name a specific ministry, agency or system. The claim has not been independently verified, and we found no public statement from Spanish authorities.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach of Spanish government systems. MortemTeam has posted a run of Latin American government leak claims in recent weeks and sells access to a lookup bot, so this set may be compiled from older leaks or several sources rather than one new intrusion. If genuine, ID document photos would raise identity-theft and fraud risk for Spanish residents.
